verdict.rationale: Zep's own Graphiti temporal knowledge graph framework documents fact invalidation and a bi-temporal model that tracks how facts change over time, which directly addresses superseding contradicted memories. However, the evidence is only a brief feature listing, with no detail on how contradictions are detected or resolved, and nothing on merging. The community note that Zep moved to graph memory because fact reconciliation was hard provides context, not proof of the behavior. Missing for 10: documented contradiction-detection and supersession mechanics, evidence of memory/entity merging or deduplication, explicit confirmation that the hosted Zep service applies this automatically, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can rely on the memory layer to update, supersede, or merge memories when new information contradicts what was stored
